paths.description: Homepage and cross-property navigation, primary discovery surface.
Azteca Noticias section listing, representative editorial index template.
Current news article, representative long-form content template.
MasterChef program hub, representative entertainment and video listing template.
Invalid route used to inspect failure and recovery treatment.

findings.summary: The site does not respect dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the default capture, and the reduced-media probe reports computed color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark surface tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Some foreground and background combinations fail contrast requirements.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility reports color-contrast as a failing audit on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the affected color tokens to meet WCAG contrast thresholds in every state.

findings.summary: Route changes have no continuity treatment.
findings.evidence: The platform probe confirms the browser supports View Transitions, while page markup contains no view-transition integration.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-origin cross-document View Transitions for section and article navigation with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long discovery surfaces do not use compositor-driven scroll cues or natural snapping.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no scroll-snap surfaces and the DOM/CSS recon found no container or view-transition integration across pages up to 9,133px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-driven progress or snap only where it clarifies position in long carousels and feeds, and respect reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long pages do not adapt navigation chrome to scroll state.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout captures show pages 3,374px to 9,133px tall, but recon found no scroll-state query or equivalent guided progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce or adapt sticky chrome after scrolling and provide a clear position or return affordance on long surfaces.

findings.summary: The notification prompt is not exposed as a named semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: The on-load prompt is visually modal, while Lighthouse reports aria-dialog-name failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the prompt with a named dialog or popover, correct focus management, Escape dismissal, and restored focus.

findings.summary: A notification opt-in interrupts content before user intent.
findings.evidence: The first mobile viewport is covered by an on-load notification prompt, and Lighthouse reports geolocation-on-start on home and notification-on-start on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove permission prompts on load. Ask only after a user invokes a feature that requires the permission.

findings.summary: Advertising and prompts delay meaningful content in the first viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile homepage first shows the permission prompt and a large PUBLICIDAD reserve before the lead story.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise editorial content above optional prompts and reduce empty ad reservations on initial mobile view.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport breakpoints rather than container context.
findings.evidence: The media probe reports no container-query rules, although the same cards appear in several differently sized modules.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable card, navigation, and media modules while retaining viewport-level page layout.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe counted 529 of 1,536 visible homepage targets below 24px in one dimension, and Lighthouse failed target-size on home and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes and spacing to at least the recommended touch size, with visible focus and hover-independent states.

findings.summary: Primary pages load too slowly.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 6.3s, TBT 1,300ms and performance 36; article LCP 6.2s, TBT 930ms and performance 40. The raw-CDP trace corroborated LCP 4.47s and five long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, delay nonessential JavaScript and ads, and break up long main-thread tasks.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers an excessive resource payload.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 371 requests and 14.63MB transferred, including 10.46MB of images and 3.70MB of scripts; 365 requests and 14.43MB were third-party by origin classification.
findings.suggestedFix: Set responsive image sizes and quality, lazy-load below-fold media, reduce variants, and gate optional third-party bundles behind intent or consent.

findings.summary: Controls and media lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed aria-dialog-name, image-alt and select-name; the homepage probe found 11 unnamed buttons and an unlabeled search input and select.
findings.suggestedFix: Add programmatic labels, meaningful alternative text, and accessible names for every dialog and icon-only control.

findings.summary: Homepage heading structure does not expose a primary heading.
findings.evidence: The homepage has zero h1 elements and starts at h3 then h4, while section, article and program templates each expose one h1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive homepage h1 and repair heading levels so sections form a coherent outline.

findings.summary: Runtime errors are emitted during normal loading.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports errors-in-console and Inspector Issues failures on both homepage and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve first-party exceptions and failed integrations, then monitor production error rates and third-party failures.

findings.summary: Image delivery is unreliable and incompletely described on editorial templates.
findings.evidence: The article mobile screenshot shows a broken lead image; image probes found six missing alt texts and six missing dimensions on the article, with similar failures on listing templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the lead image URL/fallback and emit width, height and meaningful alt text from the CMS for every editorial image.

findings.summary: Permission requests occur before a relevant user action and deprecated APIs remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports geolocation-on-start on home, notification-on-start on article, and a deprecation warning on both.
findings.suggestedFix: Request permissions in context after activation and replace deprecated browser APIs identified by DevTools.

findings.summary: Key defensive response headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. HSTS is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The page exposes visitors to an unusually broad tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe observed 69 third-party origins and 12 known trackers. HAR attributed 365 of 371 requests and 14.43MB to third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit vendor necessity, load optional analytics and ads only after consent, and enforce a strict third-party performance and privacy budget.

findings.summary: Cookie and browser policies are weak.
findings.evidence: Cookie inspection found all 15 observed cookies flagged insecure, many SameSite=None, and several 366 to 400 days old; Lighthouse observed 21 to 22 third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark HTTPS cookies Secure, use SameSite=Lax or Strict where possible, shorten retention, and remove obsolete identifiers.

findings.summary: Search and select fields lack explicit labels and autofill hints.
findings.evidence: Across four representative templates the search field has no label, aria-label or autocomplete value; the homepage select is also unlabeled.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate visible labels, provide search semantics and appropriate autocomplete tokens, and retain clear instructions.

findings.summary: Network and media cost is disproportionate to initial content.
findings.evidence: The homepage transfers 14.63MB across 371 requests, with 10.46MB images, 3.70MB scripts and 69 third-party origins. Sixty-eight below-fold images are not lazy-loaded and 70 are oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish byte and vendor budgets, lazy-load below-fold assets, right-size responsive images, and remove low-value third parties.

findings.summary: The initial JavaScript heap is heavy for a content discovery page.
findings.evidence: Heap summary recorded 1,289,194 nodes and 77.17MB self size at baseline; after repeated scrolling it recorded 1,313,414 nodes and 78.76MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce loaded widgets and vendor runtimes, virtualise only genuinely unbounded lists, and profile retained objects by constructor.

findings.summary: The presentation does not adapt to increased-contrast preference.
findings.evidence: Default, dark and prefers-contrast: more screenshots have identical byte sizes and appearance, while Lighthouse also finds insufficient contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Add prefers-contrast and forced-colors treatments that strengthen boundaries and preserve system colours.

findings.summary: Scrollable navigation and long content do not offer natural gesture constraints.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no scroll-snap surface, while long horizontally scrollable navigation is present in the DOM/CSS recon.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll snap and overscroll containment where a bounded carousel or navigation strip benefits from it.

findings.summary: Permission prompts use interruption before intent rather than contextual consent.
findings.evidence: The first viewport asks users to activate notifications before they have engaged with content; Lighthouse also detects permission requests on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Move every permission request behind an explicit, feature-relevant user action and offer a balanced decline path.

findings.summary: Touch-target sizing undermines inclusive reflow and mobile operation.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails target-size on home and article, and the mobile DOM probe counts 529 targets below 24px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target area and spacing, then verify at narrow widths and browser zoom.

findings.summary: Nonessential background network and script work is excessive.
findings.evidence: HAR records 371 requests, 71 scripts and 48 XHR/fetch requests during initial observation, while the trace records five long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer vendor work until visible or requested, batch analytics, and stop background activity when hidden.

findings.summary: Permissions are requested out of context.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports geolocation-on-start on the homepage and notification-on-start on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Request permissions only after a user activates the related feature; prefer modern credential flows for optional account access.

findings.summary: Image assets are substantially oversized and eagerly loaded.
findings.evidence: The homepage image probe reports 70 oversized images and 68 below-fold images without lazy loading; HAR records 10.46MB of images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit accurate srcset/sizes, lower quality where appropriate, and lazy-load all noncritical images.

taskList.title: Cut initial image, script and third-party cost
Add secure headers and cookie defaults
Repair accessible names, contrast and target sizes
Fix editorial image reliability and metadata
Reduce the runtime and heap footprint
Add modern navigation continuity and scroll guidance
